datasets.name: Sentinel-1 SAR imagery
datasets.verbatim: This study used SAR amplitude data from the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellite constellation.

datasets.name: SRTM V3 Digital Elevation Model
datasets.verbatim: The SRTM V3 product is provided by NASA JPL at a resolution of 1 arc-second, which is approximately a 30 m resolution.

datasets.name: Historical landslide inventory
datasets.source: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan, previous researchers, and field survey reports
datasets.verbatim: The historical landslide data were collected mainly from scientific papers published by the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan, previous researchers, and partly from field survey reports.

methods.name: Classification and Regression Tree (CART) with differential spectral indices and amplitude ratio change
methods.summary: The method uses a Classification and Regression Tree (CART) on Google Earth Engine to detect landslides by combining multitemporal Sentinel-1 SAR amplitude ratio changes and Sentinel-2 differential spectral indices (rdNDVI, dBSI, dBI). It incorporates slope and curvature filtering to reduce false positives and classifies landslide types based on the magnitude of these indices.
methods.verbatim: The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author, Sartsin Phakdimek, upon reasonable request. https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1MQLMHsOOTB_aQKAEWl4k1VpZgT_1f8FR?usp=share_link

reproducibility_assessment: The Sentinel-1 and SRTM datasets are publicly accessible via standard providers, but the historical landslide inventory is not linked or referenced with a persistent identifier. No code is provided with link, and data support the findings is provided via a Google Drive link, but upon request.
